description: Astronomy takes you outside under the night sky: observing safely, light pollution, telescopes and binoculars, constellations, planets, the Moon and Sun, an observing activity and careers or hobbies in astronomy.

safety.note: Never look at the Sun without proper solar filters. Observe at night with a buddy and dress for the cold.

versions.label: Checked against official scouting.org excerpts (partial verification)

provenance.notes: Requirement numbering and topics were checked against excerpts of official Scouting America pages (scouting.org) returned by a search index on 2026-10-24. The pages themselves could not be opened from the build environment, so wording was not compared word for word and some sub-items may be summarized from partial excerpts. Summaries are ScoutPath's own words.

references.label: Official merit badge page (scouting.org Merit Badge Hub)

requirements.title: Safety
requirements.summary: Hazards of astronomy activities, first aid, clothing for night and cold, and safe solar observing.

requirements.title: Light and air pollution
requirements.summary: How light and air pollution affect observing.

requirements.title: Telescopes and binoculars
requirements.summary: Types of telescopes and binoculars, their parts and their care.

requirements.title: The night sky
requirements.summary: Naked-eye constellations and stars, sketching a constellation, and the Milky Way.

requirements.title: Planets
requirements.summary: Visible planets, when they can be seen, how they move, and observing one.

requirements.title: The Moon
requirements.summary: Sketching the Moon and its phases, what keeps it in orbit, and eclipses.

requirements.title: The Sun and stars
requirements.summary: What the Sun is made of, sunspots, and star colors.

requirements.title: Observing activities
requirements.summary: An option such as a planetarium or observatory visit, an observing session, a star party or astrophotography.

requirements.title: Careers or hobbies
requirements.summary: One option: astronomy careers, or a hobby that uses astronomy skills.
